newsitem.title: UK: Shell awards North Sea service contracts.
newsitem.headline: Shell awards North Sea service contracts.

text.p: Shell U.K. Exploration and Production, which operates in the North Sea on behalf of Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon, said on Tuesday it planned to award service contracts worth 650 million sterling ($1.1 billion) over the next seven years.

The contracts, which should be finalised within the next two to three months and take effect early in 1998, are planned for Wood Group Engineering, AMEC Process and Energy Ltd and a joint venture between Haliburton unit Brown and Root and Arabian Oil Co International, Shell said.

It added that the "integrated service contracts" would simplify the company's engineering and operations services in the Central and Northern North Sea, combining design, maintenance and facilities modifications and resulting in substantial cost savings.

"We believe there is potential for significantly improved effectiveness giving at least 15 percent savings in engineering and maintenance costs over the next few years, which will be vital to prolong field life, in many cases to 2010 and beyond," said Shell Expro's oil and technical services director Malcolm Brinded.

The new awards, which should secure jobs for about 2,000 skilled workers in the North Sea oil industry, will each cover a number of platforms and could be extended for the entire life of the facilities, Shell said.

One award planned for Wood Group Engineering covers the four platforms in the Brent field while another planned for AMEC Process and Energy Ltd cover the other five Shell Expro operated platforms in the East Shetland Basin, namely Dunlin, Cormorant Alpha, North Cormorant, Tern and Eider.
The third, planned for Brown and Root AOC Ltd, covers facilities in the central North Sea including Fulmar, Auk, Gannet, Kittiwake and the Anasuria floating production storage and offtake vessel.

McDermott Engineering (Europe ltd) and APG/Salamis Joint Venture Ltd, who together with AMEC currently hold service contracts for some of Shell's northern platforms, are not included in the list of award winners.

The Ango-Dutch oil giant said the contracts would provide greater scope for improved safety and environmental performance and should enhance the group's efforts to remain the major operator in the North Sea for the long term future.

"The introduction of these contracts will lead to a much better coordination and integration of maintenance and engineering activities across Shell Expro," said Tony Brown, engineering manager for the Brent field.
